title: Accounts, workspaces and roles
request: A team of about 1,000 needs to know who acts and to keep each team's work apart. Add sign-in, sessions, workspaces with members and the four roles, enforced on every route; a gate approval records who approved; the company's identity provider (OIDC) is the main sign-in path, with groups mapped to roles.
spec: Password sign-in hashed with argon2, a server-side session in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie, the CSRF token kept on writes; every project, draft and session belongs to a workspace; roles enforced in one dependency; OIDC with groups mapped to roles; sessions in the database; one test per write route that the wrong role and the wrong workspace are refused. Done when a viewer cannot run a stage or approve a gate, a user never sees another workspace, and a test covers every write route.
plan: Map the auth scope (an explore agent) and ask the owner the choices the plan left open: when sign-in is required, which role names, who approves a stage's choice, which new screens may be added to the frozen demo.

Part A: roles, the accounts store (users, members, sessions, API tokens; only hashes of tokens stored), migration 0012, a request context naming the workspace's Services, a pool of Services per workspace, the guard added by the shared Router to every route from its method and path, password sign-in and the accounts routes, and python -m dclab_rnd.accounts add for the first owner.
Test every write route as a member whose role may not and as a member of another workspace using this one's ids; gate, review, fix, commit part A.

Part B: OIDC discovery, authorization code with PKCE, a signed ten-minute state cookie, the ID token checked against the provider's keys, groups mapped to roles per workspace; tested against a fake provider.

Part C: the sign-in page, the workspace switcher and avatar, Members and API tokens tabs on Admin, the roles table marked enforced, /mcp acting in the token's workspace; checked in the browser with a local test account.
Review B and C, fix, gate, commit; then fix the CI failure of the second-workspace test.

decisions.decision: Sign-in only when configured: with DCLAB_AUTH unset the app stays today's single owner on this machine; password or OIDC turns accounts on and needs PostgreSQL.
decisions.why: The owner's choice: local development and every existing test keep working unchanged, while a team deployment turns accounts on.

decisions.decision: Show the Admin page's role names (Owner, ML engineer, Reviewer, Business viewer) and store the plan's values (owner, data_scientist, reviewer, viewer).
decisions.why: The owner chose the names the product already shows; 'Intern' stays the agent, not a person's role.

decisions.decision: A stage's choice may be approved by ML engineers, reviewers and owners; gates only by reviewers and owners; gate switches, the training opt-in and members only by owners.
decisions.why: The owner's choice: the person running a project confirms its stage choices, while sign-offs that guard the holdout need a reviewer.

decisions.decision: The role check is added by the shared Router from each route's method and path, not written per route.
decisions.why: A new route cannot be left out by forgetting a decorator; the test of every write route proves the table.

decisions.decision: An existing account is linked to an OIDC identity by email only when the provider verified that email and the account has no other subject.
decisions.why: An email a person can type at the provider is not proof of who they are; linking on it allowed an account takeover (finding B1).

change: New dclab_rnd/accounts/ (roles, principal, argon2 passwords, store, guard, api, oidc, __main__), dclab_rnd/context.py, agentic/pool.py and current.py, migrations 0012 (sessions, API tokens) and 0013 (unique OIDC subject). The shared Router adds the permission check to every route; the middleware identifies the person from the session cookie or a Bearer API token and checks the request token on writes; one Services per workspace with its own stores, gateway, lessons, jobs, audit and worker, chosen per request; code holding one workspace's stores reaches the request's through stand-ins; gate approvals and the audit name the person. Part C: sign-in page, switcher and avatar, Members and API tokens tabs, roles marked enforced, a project's team from members, /mcp in the token's workspace. Tests: test_accounts, test_oidc.

findings.defect: With DCLAB_AUTH=password, signed-in users got 401 on every page outside /api/.
findings.scenario: Owner signed in, GET /, /guide, /classic and /favicon.ico all returned 401: the product shell could not load in a browser, signed in or not.
findings.cause: The middleware identified the caller only for /api/ and /mcp paths, while the Router gave the page shells a read check.
findings.fix: Identify the caller on every path except /static/, and make the four page shells public (they hold no data; every API call they make is checked).

findings.defect: The Home agent of every workspace except the server's own was bound to the server's own workspace.
findings.scenario: As owner of a second workspace, POST /api/drafts returned 201 but the agent never spoke (the error was swallowed in the background task), and POST /api/drafts/{id}/pack raised KeyError, a 500; model use would have been charged to the first workspace's budget and routing.
findings.cause: draft/api.py read services.draft_work once when the routes were registered, capturing the default workspace's stores and gateway.
findings.fix: work_now() reads services.draft_work on every call; nothing is kept from registration.
findings.test: test_the_home_agent_and_the_jobs_of_a_second_workspace_run_there (the agent speaks, the pack is 200, an upload's pipeline reaches ready).

findings.defect: Jobs of other workspaces never ran under an external worker and were not recovered after a restart.
findings.scenario: Under make dev (DCLAB_WORKER=external) with password sign-in, a member of a second workspace runs a stage: the job stays queued for ever, because the worker process opened only its own folder's workspace and claims filter by workspace.
findings.cause: Workers were started per workspace only when a job was queued in that process.
findings.fix: Pool.start_all opens every workspace and starts its worker; the server's lifespan and python -m dclab_rnd.worker call it, the worker again every 60 s.

findings.defect: tests/test_accounts.py failed when run a second time on the same database.
findings.scenario: The parallel runner reuses slot databases; a second run saved the lesson with the fixed id 'lw1abc', which belonged to the previous run's workspace, so setUpClass raised KeyError.
findings.cause: setUpClass never emptied the test database.
findings.fix: setUpClass empties the database before building the app.
findings.test: test_accounts passes twice in a row on the same database.

findings.defect: FastAPI's own schema and docs routes skipped the guard.
findings.scenario: With accounts on, an anonymous GET /openapi.json returned 200 with the whole API schema.
findings.cause: Those routes are not built by the shared Router.
findings.fix: With accounts on, the app is built without openapi_url, docs_url and redoc_url.

findings.defect: The fix for A3 let one database blip stop the worker process, and one broken workspace stop the server from starting.
findings.scenario: PostgreSQL is away for a moment when the worker's once-a-minute start_all lists the workspaces: the error leaves main() and the process exits, so jobs in every workspace stay queued; a workspace whose folder names another workspace aborts the server's lifespan and leaves the later workspaces without a worker.
findings.cause: start_all had no exception handling, unlike the worker's own loops.
findings.fix: start_all wraps the listing and each workspace's opening in its own try, reports the workspace id and the error type, and carries on; a failed workspace is retried on the next call. The Router also collects every method's permission and requires each one.

findings.defect: OIDC sign-in linked accounts on any email claim: an account takeover.
findings.scenario: A password owner owns the server's workspace and a second, unmapped workspace. An identity-provider user with another subject, group 'everyone' and an unverified email claim equal to the owner's email signs in: /api/auth/me shows the owner, switching into the second workspace returns 200 with role owner, and the group sync demotes the real owner to viewer, leaving the workspace with no owner.
findings.cause: sign_in linked on the email claim without checking email_verified and overwrote a subject already linked.
findings.fix: Find by subject first; link by email only when the provider verified it and the account has no other subject; otherwise refuse ('linked to another sign-in'); a new user gets the claimed email only when verified, else a placeholder; a partial unique index on the subject (migration 0013).

findings.defect: A role mapping naming a workspace that does not exist made every sign-in a 500 with partial writes.
findings.scenario: DCLAB_OIDC_ROLES='ml-team=data_scientist,ml-team=wnope:viewer': each sign-in by a member of ml-team raised a foreign-key violation after the user was created, with some memberships changed and others not.
findings.cause: Mapped workspaces were never checked, and each membership change was its own transaction in arbitrary order.
findings.fix: Unknown mapped workspaces are refused with a 503 before the redirect; membership changes run in one transaction, in sorted order, ending sessions and tokens of a workspace the person left.

findings.defect: Provider failures and odd inputs became 500s instead of the refusal page.
findings.scenario: The key endpoint returning 503 raised HTTPStatusError out of the callback; an email claim 'not-an-email' raised AccountError; a non-ASCII state made compare_digest raise TypeError.
findings.fix: Provider steps wrap network, value, key, type and attribute errors into OidcError; sign_in wraps account and integrity errors; state, nonce and MAC are compared as bytes; a malformed JWK or token is refused too.
findings.test: test_oidc covers a key endpoint returning 503 and a non-ASCII state.

findings.defect: An issuer ending in '/' refused every sign-in.
findings.scenario: Providers such as Auth0 publish an issuer with a trailing slash and put it in iss; the token was verified against the stripped value, giving 403 InvalidIssuerError.
findings.cause: config() stripped the slash and passed that value to the token check.
findings.fix: Discovery compares stripped forms, but iss is checked against the provider's published issuer exactly.
findings.test: The test issuer now ends in '/'.

findings.defect: Sign-ins and the role changes made by the group sync were not audited.
findings.scenario: A sign-in that adds, changes or removes a membership wrote nothing, while the same change on the Members routes wrote role_change.
findings.cause: The sync path had no audit call.
findings.fix: Every sign-in (password and OIDC) and each membership change from groups are written to that workspace's audit.

findings.defect: The client secret was sent in HTTP Basic without form-encoding.
findings.scenario: A secret containing '%', '+' or ':' fails on providers that decode it as RFC 6749 requires.
findings.fix: Both values are form-encoded; azp is required to equal the client when aud lists several audiences; DCLAB_OIDC_REDIRECT is required behind HTTPS.

findings.defect: A new API token stayed in the page after its dialog closed.
findings.scenario: Create a token and click 'Copy and close': the secret stays as hidden text in the modal body until another dialog replaces it.
findings.cause: modal.close() only removed the open class.
findings.test: Re-checked in the source and the rebuilt static app; no other dialog reads its inputs after closing.

findings.defect: The token name was escaped twice in the dialog title.
findings.scenario: A token named 'R&D laptop' showed as 'R&D laptop: copy it now'.
findings.cause: The title was escaped and then set as text.
findings.fix: Pass the name unescaped, since the title is set with textContent.

findings.defect: The sign-in page showed any text passed in the address as an error.
findings.scenario: A link with ?signin_error=Your password expired, send it to ... puts an attacker's message on DCLab's own sign-in page.
findings.cause: showSignIn read signin_error from the URL, though nothing in the server sets it.
findings.fix: The sign-in page shows only the app's own note.

findings.defect: On CI the second-workspace test never saw the Home agent's first message.
findings.scenario: The test passed in a second locally but failed on GitHub's runner with six test files at once; raising the wait from 30 s to 120 s did not help.
findings.cause: The signed-in test clients were never entered, so each request ran on an event loop that closed with the response; the Home agent started as a task on that loop and on a busy runner was cancelled before it began. Under uvicorn the loop outlives the request, so the product was fine.
findings.fix: The draft is created through the client entered in setUpClass, with the second owner's session.

measurements.name: agent judgment suite after the validator change
measurements.gate: A change to studio/graph.py needs a fresh make agent-eval whose scores match the previous result (the prompt gate's rule).
measurements.result: AEV-010 scores the same as AEV-009.

outcome: Done in three parts: accounts, sessions, API tokens and the four roles checked on every route (A); sign-in through the company's identity provider with groups mapped to roles (B); the sign-in page, switcher, Members and API tokens tabs, and /mcp in the token's workspace (C). Without DCLAB_AUTH nothing changes. Left open: an owner can add an existing user without that user's consent; a group change reaches DCLab at the next sign-in; a sign-in that removes a workspace's last owner is allowed.
lessons: A test that only checks refusals cannot see that allowed users are refused too; test the allowed path on every kind of route.
Never capture per-request services at registration time; in a multi-workspace server that binds everyone to the first workspace.
Linking identities by an unverified email is an account takeover; trust only the provider's subject and a verified email.
When a test fails only on a busy CI runner, longer waits are not a fix until the cause is known; here the event loop was closing under the task.
A fix that adds a periodic call must keep the loop's existing tolerance of a database that is briefly away.
